constraints: Backward compatibility with existing artifacts — all Pydantic fields must have defaults
Raw SDK clients for gap analysis + content engine (no LangChain wrappers)
OpenRouter via openai SDK (AsyncOpenAI/OpenAI with base_url override, max_retries=0)
LangGraph >=1.0 interrupt model: check __interrupt__ in result dict, not GraphInterrupt exception
Double-underscore separator for effective slugs: {company}__{product}
Default-deny middleware — all routes protected unless explicitly whitelisted
core/ cannot import from api/ — shared code goes in core/shared_tools/
DATABASE_URL is REQUIRED — no JSON fallback for TaskStore, AuthService, or Topic Discovery
REDIS_URL is REQUIRED — no in-memory fallback for EventBus or checkpointer
Topic Discovery pipeline is DB-only — TopicDiscoveryStorage no longer used in pipeline hot paths
Pipeline B uses additive per-subdomain writes (db_write_assignments_for_subdomain), NOT delete-all + re-insert-all
Pipeline B expansion uses allow_parallel=True — no Redis slug lock; concurrency via db_claim_subdomain_for_expansion (optimistic DB lock)
Stuck 'expanding' nodes auto-reset after 20 minutes (claim_for_expansion stale threshold)
tree_json set NULL during expansion; rebuilt after batch; db_read_taxonomy falls back to flat-node reconstruction
pipeline_state.json only written when Redis is unavailable (Redis is primary CE state store)
Async Redis for hot paths (pipeline writes), sync Redis for locks + sync readers
Distributed locks are fail-closed when Redis is configured (no split-brain fallback)
CSP strict-dynamic disabled in dev (blocks Next.js HMR)
handleUnauthorized must skip redirect when on auth pages (prevents loop)
useSearchParams() requires Suspense boundary in Next.js 14 App Router
OPENROUTER_API_KEY is REQUIRED for Content Engine, Topic Discovery, Perplexity research, CE-0 Planner, AP-1 Suggester, GA-S8 Report, GA Perplexity Engine
VSG-1 author discovery stays on litellm (Anthropic web_search_20250305 tool not supported by OpenRouter)
Gap analysis engines (Claude/Gemini/OpenAI) stay on native SDKs (web search / grounding / reasoning not supported by OpenRouter)
GA Perplexity engine NOW on OpenRouter (Phase 2) — AsyncPerplexity no longer used
TD-entry Content Engine now has a durable topic-run foundation — every durable runtime row/event must carry both topic_assignment_id and display_id
TD gap-analysis start no longer uses company-level slug exclusivity; global concurrency is still bounded by the Redis semaphore
Company-wide SSE transport now uses Redis Streams in production; process-local company fanout is test-only
Durable TD-entry topic-run updates must target a stable run identity (task-scoped for GA binding, ga_run-scoped for production) — never fall back to the latest row for the same topic_assignment_id
Durable production stage writes must occur at true execution points (after semaphore acquisition), not optimistically in the HTTP request handler

Brief-level CE stage writes for TD-entry now propagate durably via brief_id + task_id + effective_slug matching; company SSE publishes authoritative topic_run_changed payloads alongside legacy state_changed hints

TD-entry rebrief/retry loops must preserve the original brief_id/display_id and thread session_factory through evaluator/worker reruns so durable topic-run updates stay attached to the same user-facing card

FastAPI startup must reconcile TD topic-run scheduler state (`queued`, `resume_queued`, `claimed`, `running`, `waiting_human`) against recovered task rows before serving traffic, and then auto-dispatch any companies with recoverable queued work

Restart repair is topic-run-led: `waiting_human` persists across restarts, stranded continuations recover to `resume_queued`, plain stranded runs recover to `content_queued`, and queued work must clear stale `pipeline_task_id` values when the referenced task is gone

Content Studio frontend now keeps a normalized topic-run store keyed by topic_run_id/topic_assignment_id/brief_id, applies topic_run_changed as the primary live overlay for TD-entry cards, uses updated_at rather than per-run seq for cross-run recency, and treats state_changed plus background polling only as reconciliation

TD-entry durable completion/failure semantics are per-topic: mixed batches preserve each card's terminal state, CE rollback mirrors durable gap_analysis_complete, and Stage 3 worker crashes emit an explicit durable failed transition
The TD-entry card log now reads directly from `content_engine_topic_events` by `topic_run_id`; `display_id` stays user-facing in the UI while `topic_run_id` remains the durable runtime identity

TD durable topic-event payloads are enriched on read with stable run context (`brief_id`, `display_id`, `topic_text`, `entry_mode`, `buyer_stage`, `intent_type`, `effective_slug`, `batch_run_id`), and human-facing runner notes for terminal/rollback semantics belong in `payload_json`

Content Studio's Activity tab is now generic at the frontend boundary (`card-activity` adapter + `useCardActivity`); manual and prompt-entry modes should plug into that contract rather than forking a second activity UI
Company SSE over Redis Streams must keep `XREAD BLOCK` below `settings.redis_socket_timeout`; idle Redis read timeouts are treated as heartbeat ticks, not fatal stream errors

Any card state that can be reconciled by polling after live updates must carry server-authored `created_at`/`updated_at`; for TD GA cards that means `write_ga_phase_state*()` must always maintain timestamped `__meta:ta-*` entries and `/content/briefs` must surface those timestamps

For local account reset / test-slate cleanup, clear the company-scoped runtime-driving tables and Redis state (`content_engine_*`, `content_pieces`, `content_artifacts`, content-engine `api_tasks`, `pipeline_state:{slug}`, and leftover task SSE keys) rather than deleting `pipeline_runs` directly; `pipeline_runs` fan out into broader analytics tables such as `run_queries` and require a separate full-graph cleanup script

TD-entry production no longer shares CE capacity across tenants: CE runners (`content`, `content_v13`, `td_content`) now use a company-scoped Redis semaphore (`API_MAX_CONCURRENT_CONTENT_ENGINE_PER_COMPANY`, default 15) keyed by `company_slug`, while singleton pipelines remain on the shared `semaphore:pipelines` pool

CE approval waits now release the active company semaphore slot and reacquire it before graph execution resumes; queued TD topics therefore compete only for truly active CE work slots, not for human-wait states

TD `start-production` now queues durable topic runs and dispatches one `td_content` task per claimed topic. Scheduler state now lives in dedicated `content_engine_topic_runs` columns (`scheduler_state`, `claim_token`, queue/claim/wait timestamps, `continuation_payload_json`) rather than `metadata_json.dispatch_state`

TD HITL-2 / HITL-3 approvals now externalize into durable continuations: the runner records `waiting_human` on the topic run, approval routes must durably queue `resume_queued` before recording approval history, and the dispatcher reuses the existing `td_content` task id to resume the LangGraph checkpoint from the stored `thread_id` and continuation payload

TD durable scheduler transitions are now the router commit point: `start-production` must fail closed unless durable topic runs were actually queued, and nullable scheduler fields like `pipeline_task_id` / `claimed_at` / `waiting_for_human_at` require explicit clear semantics on requeue

After the 2026-04-10 resume-loop incident, stale Redis brief-card task mappings (`WE-*` / `__tid:WE-*`) were proven to outlive the authoritative durable `content_engine_topic_runs.pipeline_task_id` after a poisoned run. Fresh TD retests should start from cleaned runtime state, and the remaining hardening gap is to repair or bypass stale Redis brief-card task ids in favor of durable topic-run identity on `/content/briefs`.
